headline: US economy grows 3.4% in Q3, exceeding expectations
summary: The U.S. economy expanded at an annualized rate of 3.4% in the third quarter of 2026, surpassing market estimates of 3.1%. Growth was driven by household spending, corporate investment, and government expenditures.
why: GDP growth is the primary indicator of economic health. For investors, stronger-than-expected growth can influence Federal Reserve interest rate policy and corporate earnings outlooks.

impacts.name: US Dollar
impacts.why: Stronger economic growth often supports the currency by signaling higher potential interest rates.

why_moved: The data beat market expectations, signaling resilience in the US economy despite inflationary pressures, which typically influences bond yields and equity valuations.
